title: Recovered SCOBY-D0 microwave-treated bacterial-cellulose oil-sorbent concept and evidence audit
research_question: Could a microwave-modified dried kombucha bacterial-cellulose pellicle be a retrievable high-capacity oil/petroleum sorbent, and how does the claim relate to candle-wick behavior?

traceable_origin.scope_of_verification: GitHub versions of specified SCOBY-D0 and Meta Registry archival files, project lineage, and research-track files. Does not establish a complete scan of legacy NAS/PC experimental recordings.

historical_microwave_arm.name: Microwave-transformed bacterial cellulose
historical_microwave_arm.concept: Investigate whether microwave treatment changes dry bacterial cellulose network morphology, wetting and sorption. Microscopic structure and actual composition have to be measured independently.
unestablished_assertions: That microwave-treated SCOBY is an ideal oil sorbent.
That visible porous or charred texture proves functional aerogel architecture.
That microwave treatment improves oil/water selectivity or crude-oil sorption relative to controls.
That the material is field-safe or environmentally non-toxic.
characterization_required: measured oil uptake and water uptake

oil_spill_product_concept.intended_use: Large retrievable porous pads or boom inserts that preferentially absorb floating oil and allow partial mechanical oil recovery.
oil_spill_product_concept.process_architecture: BC production -> controlled washing/formation -> pore-preserving processing -> selectivity screening -> retrievable sorbent pad -> controlled oil recovery/waste management.
oil_spill_product_concept.critical_difference: Dry, compacted BioPapyrus optimizes coherent paper-like sheet structure; oil-sorbent architecture generally needs pore volume and selective wetting.
oil_spill_product_concept.native_bc_constraint: Wet/raw bacterial cellulose is strongly hydrophilic and is not proven to preferentially sorb oil when immersed in water.

proposed_comparison.D0: Pressed air-dried dense sheet: low-porosity control.
proposed_comparison.D3: Freeze-dried modified BC: oil-over-water selectivity performance lead (requires leachate validation).
proposed_comparison.D4: Controlled carbonized BC aerogel: advanced laboratory route.
proposed_comparison.D5: Microwave-transformed BC: material identity investigation; not validated for use.

source_program_scenarios.note: These are design targets / model scenarios from historical project files, not measured D5 outcomes.

cedre_compatible_internal_prescreen.note: An internal prescreen aligned with a received Cedre testing protocol, not Cedre validation.

quantitative_evidence_boundaries.exact_conclusion: No sample-level raw mass or oil/water data supporting 'ideal sorbent' were identified in the reviewed files.

literature_context.statement: Selected engineered bacterial-cellulose aerogels and carbonized/modified composites have published high oil uptake in laboratory conditions.

reported_external_literature_ranges.source: SCOBY-D0 2233 archive cites 2024 hydrophobic BC aerogel

literature_context.limits: Secondary summaries recorded in project artifacts; do not transfer figures to untreated or microwaved SCOBY-D0. Original publications and test definitions must be checked before public performance claims.

relation_to_candle_fire.possible_shared_mechanism: Porosity and liquid wetting can affect both sorption and capillary uptake of molten wax.
relation_to_candle_fire.non_equivalence: Oil-uptake capacity after soaking is not a continuous capillary flux toward a heated candle flame. Oil retention and wax throughput can demand different pore structures and wettability.
relation_to_candle_fire.open_test: Only characterize uncontaminated, known-composition samples under controlled materials testing before any supervised candle-wick comparison.
relation_to_candle_fire.forbidden_inference: Never assume petroleum-loaded or contaminated sorbent is appropriate wick material.

next_scientific_gate.proposed_safe_initial_step: Locate authenticated legacy datasets/photos with sample identities, masses and protocol, or perform matched non-flame sorption screening using an innocuous oil surrogate under appropriate laboratory controls.
quantities: mass after reproducible oil loading and drainage
next_scientific_gate.advancement_rule: Do not label D5 'ideal', superior, or field-ready without preregistered independent repeatable measurements against appropriate commercial baselines and environmental testing.

reasons: Dry cellulose may experience hot spots, smoke, arcing, charring and ignition.
Unknown residues, glycerol, flammable solvents or oil contamination can lead to hazardous heating/decomposition.
Petroleum-contaminated sorbent requires safe collection and licensed handling.
